paper.title_en: The deci-Hz gravitational wave signal from the collapse of rotating very massive stars
paper.abstract_en: We calculate the gravitational wave signal from the collapse of a rotating 300 $M_\odot$ star just above the upper end of the pair-instability supernova regime. The large-scale asymmetries that develop during the collapse produce a strong signal in the deci-Hz range that has a characteristic shape that is likely amenable to a template-based search. Although tempered by the low incidence of nearby astrophysical candidates, the most ambitious designs for deci-Hz detectors could detect such signals out to distances of ~250 Mpc, possibly at a rate of 0.3 per year. Additional numerical modeling is required to refine these rate estimates, however. We also demonstrate that proposed deci-Hz GW observation missions, even without confident single-source detections, could be used to provide information about the population of astrophysical candidates and, in particular, constrain the initial mass function of very massive stars.
